issues.legal_issue: A coparcener's inter vivos gift of an undivided interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property is generally invalid and does not make the donee a successor by devolution in a pending suit.
material_facts: The deceased had claimed a specific share in the coparcenary property by filing a partition suit and was treated as divided in status from the other coparceners.
During his lifetime, he executed a registered gift deed purporting to give his coparcenary interest to the claimant and put her in possession of land.
The claimant relied on the gift to seek substitution as a person who had acquired the deceased's interest during the pending appeal.
issues.conclusion: The gift was not a valid transfer of the deceased's coparcenary interest, and the claimant acquired no interest by devolution under it to qualify for substitution on that basis.
issues.legal_principle: Section 30 of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956 permits testamentary disposition of a coparcener's interest; a testamentary disposition takes effect after death, unlike an inter vivos gift, which takes effect during the donor's lifetime under Section 123 of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882. A coparcener's inter vivos gift of an undivided interest is generally void except where the gift is made with the consent of the other coparceners, is between coparceners, or falls within an exceptional circumstance. Order 22 Rule 10 CPC permits substitution of a person who acquires an interest by devolution during the suit, but the invalid gift conferred no such interest. The Court relied on Jalaja Shedthi v. Lakshmi Shedthi and Phoolchand v. Gopal Lal on severance of status, and on the authorities concerning the invalidity of inter vivos gifts of coparcenary interests, including Baba v. Thimma, Dwarampudi Nagaratnamba v. Kunuku Ramayya, Venkata Subbammana v. Rathnamma, and Mukund Singh v. Wazir Singh.

rule.if: pending_suit_substitution_claim and substitution_claim_based_on_inter_vivos_gift and gift_of_undivided_coparcenary_interest and not (other_coparceners_consented or gift_between_coparceners or exceptional_valid_gift)

predicates.pending_suit_substitution_claim: A person seeks substitution in a pending suit or appeal on the basis that an interest in the disputed property devolved to that person during the proceeding.
predicates.substitution_claim_based_on_inter_vivos_: The claimant relies on a transfer intended to take effect during the transferor's lifetime.
predicates.gift_of_undivided_coparcenary_interest: The transfer purports to give away the transferor's undivided interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property.
predicates.other_coparceners_consented: The other coparceners consented to the gift.
predicates.gift_between_coparceners: The gift was made to another coparcener.
predicates.exceptional_valid_gift: The gift falls within an exceptional circumstance in which such a transfer is valid.

issues.definition: When a substitution claim in a pending proceeding rests on an inter vivos gift of an undivided coparcenary interest, and none of the stated grounds for validity applies, the donee is not entitled to substitution as a successor by devolution.

issues.legal_issue: A daughter who is established to be a surviving Class I heir succeeds to the deceased coparcener's interest under the statutory succession rule and may represent the estate in a pending partition appeal.
material_facts: The deceased coparcener's daughter sought substitution in the pending partition appeal.
Oral evidence from eleven witnesses supported her claim of paternity; the deceased had also identified her as his daughter in the genealogy accompanying the partition plaint and in the gift deed.
The High Court rejected her claim, relying in part on a discrepancy in her husband's name and an entry in a private record concerning a tonsuring ceremony.
The deceased's interest in the coparcenary property was subject to the statutory rule that applies when a surviving female Class I relative exists.
issues.conclusion: The evidence established that the claimant was the deceased's daughter and Class I heir; she succeeded to his interest and was entitled to be substituted to represent his estate under Order 22 Rule 3 CPC.
issues.legal_principle: Under the proviso to Section 6(1) of the Hindu Succession Act, 1956, when a male Hindu dies with an interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property and leaves a surviving female relative specified in Class I of the Schedule, that interest devolves by testamentary or intestate succession rather than by survivorship. Explanation 1 to Section 6 deems the deceased's interest to be the share that would have been allotted to him on a partition immediately before his death. A daughter who succeeds to that interest may represent the estate under Order 22 Rule 3 CPC. On the evidence, a private record does not carry the same weight as a public document, and the Court found no adequate basis to reject the substantial oral evidence and the deceased's own identification of the claimant as his daughter.

rule.if: pending_partition_appeal and deceased_had_coparcenary_interest and claimant_proved_to_be_daughter and claimant_is_surviving_class_i_heir and no_valid_testamentary_disposition

predicates.pending_partition_appeal: A partition appeal remains pending when a party dies and substitution is sought.
predicates.deceased_had_coparcenary_interest: The deceased held an interest in Mitakshara coparcenary property at death.
predicates.claimant_proved_to_be_daughter: Evidence establishes that the claimant is the deceased's daughter.
predicates.claimant_is_surviving_class_i_heir: The claimant is a surviving female relative included in Class I of the succession schedule.
predicates.no_valid_testamentary_disposition: No valid testamentary disposition governs the deceased's interest.

issues.definition: If a deceased party in a pending partition appeal had a coparcenary interest and the claimant is proved to be his surviving Class I daughter, with no valid testamentary disposition, the claimant is entitled to substitution as representative of the estate.
